title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization - Nature Energy
gist: Xi'an Jiaotong University and CAS Institute of Physics researchers use the cyclic ether 1,3-dioxane (DOX) as an electrolyte solvent for anode-free sodium batteries. DOX coordinates weakly with Na+, which aids reversible plating, and its controlled oligomerization forms a thin, robust SEI. ~300 mAh pouch cells keep ~80% capacity after 1,400 cycles at 1 C and 88% at −40 °C. Only the abstract and front matter are available; the full text is paywalled.

insights.claim: Anode-free sodium batteries offer a promising route to low-cost, high-energy-density energy storage, but irreversible sodium loss during cycling limits their practical use.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Fixing sodium loss would unlock a cheaper, lithium-free storage chemistry with higher energy density.
insights.quote: offer a promising route to low cost, high-energy-density energy storage

insights.claim: A molecular-level electrolyte design based on the cyclic ether 1,3-dioxane (DOX) reduces sodium loss in anode-free sodium batteries by making sodium deposition highly reversible while also suppressing electrolyte decomposition.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: An electrolyte-only fix can be adopted in existing cell production without changing electrodes.

insights.claim: Weak coordination between DOX and Na+ ions makes Na+ desolvation easier, which supports reversible sodium deposition.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Weakly solvating electrolytes are a general design principle for metal-anode chemistries.
insights.quote: Weak coordination of DOX with Na+ facilitates Na+ desolvation

insights.claim: Controlled oligomerization of DOX forms a thin, robust solid–electrolyte interphase that stops continuous electrolyte decomposition and stabilizes sodium plating and stripping.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Using solvent reactivity in a controlled way to build the SEI can replace costly functional additives.
insights.quote: controlled DOX oligomerization forms a thin and robust solid–electrolyte interphase

insights.claim: The study links DOX's behaviour to its ring strain and solvation structure.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Ring strain gives solvent screening a quantitative handle for electrolyte formulators.

insights.claim: 300-mAh-class anode-free sodium pouch cells with a cathode loading of about 20 mg cm−2 retained about 80% capacity after 1,400 cycles at 1 C using the DOX electrolyte.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Hundreds of cycles to 1,400 at practical loading moves anode-free sodium toward commercially relevant cycle life.
insights.quote: retain ~80% capacity after 1,400 cycles at 1 C

insights.claim: The DOX-electrolyte anode-free sodium pouch cells run at rates up to 3 C and achieve round-trip energy efficiency up to about 98%.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: High round-trip efficiency matters for grid-storage economics.
insights.quote: operate at rates up to 3 C

insights.claim: The DOX-electrolyte anode-free sodium pouch cells keep 88% of their capacity at −40 °C.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Low-temperature performance gives sodium an advantage over LFP in cold-climate storage and vehicles.

insights.claim: The anode-free sodium pouch cells were tested as Al@C||NFPP cells, with no pre-loaded sodium metal anode, so sodium plates directly onto the Al@C anode-side substrate against an NFPP cathode.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Having no excess sodium anode is the configuration that gives anode-free cells their cost and density advantage.

insights.claim: The work comes from Xi'an Jiaotong University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Physics (Yong-Sheng Hu's group), with funding from the National Natural Science Foundation of China and a CAS strategic priority programme.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
entities: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
National Natural Science Foundation of China
insights.so_what: Chinese state-backed labs keep leading sodium-battery R&D, consistent with China's lead in sodium-ion commercialization.
